claims.text: Solid-solution alloys containing at least five elements in equal or near-equal atomic percentages have high configurational entropy.
The proposed starting nanoparticles are 5–20 nm homogeneous, single-phase solid solutions.
Configurational entropy is the primary factor governing structural and chemical stability of equiatomic five-metal nanoparticles.
High mixing entropy causes sluggish atomic diffusion.
Entropy-mediated sluggish diffusion maintains a single-phase solid solution at high temperature.
The nanoparticles should remain single-phase throughout 473–1923 K, including under reactive atmospheres, unless surface or interfacial effects become dominant.
High surface-to-volume ratios make surface and interfacial energy effects more pronounced in very small nanoparticles.
Under reactive conditions, surface and interfacial energies can lower kinetic barriers and drive elemental partitioning.
If entropy dominates, the lattice will exhibit only minor thermal expansion over 473–1923 K.
If entropy dominates, the constituent elements will remain spatially uniform over 473–1923 K.
Secondary phases or compositional heterogeneity should emerge only when interfacial effects overcome entropic stabilization.
Nanoparticles substantially smaller than 5 nm may segregate at lower temperatures.
Reactive environments that significantly alter surface energies may induce segregation at lower temperatures.
Peak splitting or new diffraction peaks can be used to detect phase formation, while spatially resolved spectroscopy can detect elemental segregation.
Secondary phases or significant elemental segregation well below 1000 K would falsify the proposed entropy-dominated stabilization mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that a reactive environment can legitimately cause segregation at lower temperatures, whereas the falsification rule treats segregation well below 1000 K under a controlled reactive ambience as falsifying. Without independently excluding a surface-energy change, the proposed falsifying observation can be absorbed by the stated exception.
